targets.authors: Cornelissen K. K., Bester A., Cairns P., Tovee M. J. and Cornelissen P. L.
targets.title: The influence of personal BMI on body size estimations ans sensitivity to body size change in anorexia spectrum disorders
targets.evidence_quote: In summary, the current study serves both as a replication and extension of Cornelissen et al. [17,18].
targets.outcome_quote: When analysing the entire clinical group, their self-estimated BMI closely matched their actual BMI, evidenced by a regression slope close to one (see Fig 2), suggesting a relatively accurate perception of own body size across the actual BMI range. However, excluding the participants with a history of bulimia nervosa and repeating the analysis, yielded results more consistent with Cornelissen et al. [17,18], as illustrated in Fig 3. Specifically, the regression slope of estimated BMI on actual BMI had a slope > 1, with accurate estimation at low actual BMI, and systematically increasing overestimation as actual BMI increased.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors describe agreement on the group-by-BMI interaction and psychological contribution, but a full clinical-group slope near one rather than the originals’ accelerating overestimation. Excluding bulimia participants restores the original pattern. The stated replication of the key interaction concerns one finding, not an overall verdict overriding the described difference.
